raw_response:
Alright, let me think through this year's plan.

---

*Sitting down with a cup of tea, looking out at the fields...*

I've been working this land 40 years. My son is in Handan now, works construction — he sends money but he's not coming back to farm. So it's just me and the wife, and she's got bad knees. 7.5 mu isn't a lot of land but at our age it's plenty.

Last few years I've done about 5 mu cotton and 2.5 mu stevia. I'll stick with that split. Cotton I know — grew it since I was a young man. Stevia came in through the cooperative maybe six, seven years back, and the price they pay is decent. They give us the seedlings and buy back the dry leaves, so at least we don't worry about selling. But stevia is hand work — cutting, drying, spreading — that's where the old lady and I spend most of our summer.

**Cotton (5 mu).** Plant around April 20th, maybe a few days later if the ground's still cold. I use the Bt variety from the agricultural station — costs more than the old seed but the bollworm doesn't eat it up. Seed runs me about 40 yuan/mu.

For fertilizer, I broadcast compound (15-15-15) before planting, about 40 kg/mu, then cover with maybe 15 kg urea as base. When the buds come out I topdress another 15 kg urea, and sometimes another round at bloom if the plants look pale. Comes out to around 15 kg N/mu total. The extension fellow a few years ago said I could get by with 12 kg, but I tried cutting back one year and the cotton just didn't fill out. Not worth the risk — fertilizer is cheap compared to losing half a picking.

Water — the well electricity bill is what gets you. I'll irrigate once before planting if it's dry (usually is in April here), once at budding, once at bloom. Three times unless the rain comes. 

Spray herbicide before planting, then bollworm sprays 2-3 times in July-August. Also put on mepiquat to keep the plants short — too tall and they fall over and it's hard to pick.

Tillage I hire — old man He down the road has a rotary tiller, 40 yuan/mu and he does it in an afternoon.

Picking is the killer. Two of us can't pick 5 mu of cotton ourselves. We hire women from the village, maybe 3-4 of them for a week each picking. That's 80 yuan/mu easy in labor.

**Stevia (2.5 mu).** The cooperative brings seedlings in late April, we transplant by hand — that's 4-5 days of bent-over work for the two of us. Less fertilizer than cotton, maybe 30 kg compound per mu plus one topdress of 10 kg urea. So around 8-9 kg N/mu. Water 2-3 times. The coop tells us not to spray much pesticide because the leaves have to be clean for the buyer — so just herbicide before transplant, and we pull weeds by hand after that. Two cuttings through summer, dry them on the threshing floor.

Yield — cotton I'm hoping for around 260 kg lint per mu, that's about what I got last year. Stevia maybe 200 kg dry leaves per mu, depends on how many cuttings we can get.

Cash-wise it's tight but manageable. The cotton subsidy helps, and stevia gives us cash in hand when the coop pays.
